message.content:
Lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus quagga) belong to two different orders—Carnivora and Perissodactyla, respectively.  
Their most recent common ancestor is the last common ancestor of the **Laurasiatheria** clade, a group of placental mammals that split from other placentals roughly 90–100 million years ago. In other words, the lion and zebra share a common ancestor at the level of the last common ancestor of all Laurasiatherian mammals.

Their common ancestor would be at the level of the last common ancestor of all placental mammals?
